title: Intermittent HTTP 429 from nightly sync job
content:
Customer issue: Business workspace saw bursts of HTTP 429 (CF-429) when a nightly job started 400 requests in the same second.

Resolution: Explained the sliding 60-second window. Customer changed the client to read Retry-After and use exponential backoff with jitter, and spread the job's requests over the minute. No more 429s.

title: Constant 429 responses after traffic growth
content:
Customer issue: Pro workspace consistently peaked at about 450 requests/min against a 300/min limit after adding a new integration.

Resolution: Usage confirmed the peak was well above the Pro limit. Customer added caching and page_size=100, which brought the peak to about 280/min. Also explained upgrading to Business (1,000/min) if growth continues.

title: 429 errors: workaround using extra API keys
content:
Customer issue: Customer on CloudFlow 4.2 hit 429 errors from one integration service.

Resolution: Because 4.2 rate limits are applied per API key, the agent advised creating a second API key and splitting traffic between two keys to double throughput. Customer confirmed the 429s stopped.

title: CF-503 errors during platform incident
content:
Customer issue: Multiple workflows failed with CF-503 for about 25 minutes.

Resolution: The status page showed a Workflow Engine incident at the time. The default 4.3 retry policy recovered most steps; the customer re-ran the 6 remaining failed runs from Workflow History after the incident was resolved.

title: CF-503 on high-concurrency workflow
content:
Customer issue: Workflow fanning out to 200 parallel runs got intermittent CF-503 on CloudFlow 4.2; the status page was green.

Resolution: Engine capacity protection rejected the burst. Customer set workflow concurrency to 20 and turned on workflow-level retries (4.2: up to 3, 30 s delay). The errors stopped.

title: Salesforce connection fails with invalid_grant
content:
Customer issue: After a Salesforce admin changed session policies, all Salesforce steps failed with CF-401 and 'invalid_grant'.

Resolution: The OAuth refresh token had been revoked. Customer clicked Integrations > Salesforce > Reconnect and authorized again, and the admin set the connected app's refresh-token policy to 'valid until revoked'. Failed runs were re-run.

title: Salesforce INVALID_LOGIN after password change
content:
Customer issue: Salesforce steps started failing with INVALID_LOGIN after the integration user's Salesforce password was changed.

Resolution: Advised the customer to re-enter the new Salesforce password and the new security token (emailed by Salesforce after the password reset) under Integrations > Salesforce. The connection was restored.

title: Slack step fails with channel_not_found
content:
Customer issue: Workflow could not post to a private Slack channel; the step error was channel_not_found.

Resolution: The CloudFlow bot wasn't a member of the private channel. Customer ran /invite @CloudFlow in the channel and re-ran the failed runs.

title: Slack missing_scope after admin policy change
content:
Customer issue: Slack messages stopped with 'missing_scope' after the customer's Slack admin reviewed app permissions.

Resolution: The chat:write scope had been removed. Customer reconnected via Integrations > Slack > Reconnect and the Slack admin approved the scopes.

title: Run fails with CF-400 on a mapped field
content:
Customer issue: Workflow failed at the 'Create invoice' step with CF-400 'amount must be a number'.

Resolution: The value came from a webhook as text. Applied the to_number filter ({{trigger.body.amount | to_number}}) and re-ran the failed runs.

title: Workflow switched off automatically
content:
Customer issue: Customer's workflow was switched Off unexpectedly.

Resolution: The workflow failed 20 times in a row because its Google Sheets connection had lost access, so it was auto-disabled. Customer shared the sheet with the connected account again and switched the workflow back On. Recommended setting up failure alerts.

title: Need to export 90 days of workflow history
content:
Customer issue: Customer needed a single export covering the last 90 days of workflow history.

Resolution: Explained that exports are limited to CSV, 30 days, and 10,000 rows, and that there is no way to export a larger range or JSON. Customer ran three consecutive 30-day CSV exports.

title: Step times out after 300 seconds
content:
Customer issue: Data-processing step consistently failed with CF-408 after 300 seconds on CloudFlow 4.2.

Resolution: On 4.2 the step timeout is fixed at 300 seconds. Customer split processing into batches of 500 rows using a loop and the 'Trigger workflow' step. Runs now complete.

title: Long-running enrichment step needs more time
content:
Customer issue: Enrichment step calling a slow external API timed out with CF-408 at 300 seconds.

Resolution: On 4.3, raised the step timeout to 600 seconds in Step settings > Timeout and raised the HTTP request timeout to 90 seconds. Confirmed the step is idempotent before relying on the default retries.

title: Failed steps are not retried
content:
Customer issue: Customer asked why transient HTTP 502 errors from their API failed the whole run.

Resolution: Explained that CloudFlow never retries failed steps automatically and there is no backoff option. Customer built a manual retry loop with a 'Delay' step and a branch.

title: Workflow runs missing from history
content:
Customer issue: Customer on the Free plan couldn't find runs from two weeks earlier.

Resolution: Free plan history retention is 7 days and older runs are permanently deleted. Support couldn't restore them. Customer upgraded to Pro (30 days) and set up regular exports.

title: Step output empty in later step
content:
Customer issue: A Slack message showed blank values for a customer tier field.

Resolution: The lookup step was in a branch that wasn't taken, so it was skipped. Customer added a default filter ({{steps.lookup.output.tier | default: "standard"}}).

title: Payment failed: card expired
content:
Customer issue: Workspace became past_due after an invoice failed with reason card_expired.

Resolution: Owner added a new card under Settings > Billing > Payment method and clicked 'Retry payment' on the failed invoice. Payment succeeded and the workspace returned to active.

title: Payment failed: authentication required
content:
Customer issue: Invoice failed with authentication_required even though the card was valid.

Resolution: The customer's bank requires 3-D Secure. Customer clicked 'Retry payment' and completed the bank verification. Payment succeeded.

title: Unexpected proration charge after upgrade
content:
Customer issue: Customer asked about an extra charge in the middle of the billing period.

Resolution: Explained that upgrading from Pro to Business charges a prorated amount for the remaining days immediately. The invoice proration line matched the 12 remaining days.

title: Possible duplicate charge
content:
Customer issue: Customer saw two card charges after retrying a failed payment.

Resolution: Only one invoice had status paid. The second item was a pending bank authorization from the failed attempt, which disappeared within 4 business days. No refund was needed.

title: Refund request for annual plan within 14 days
content:
Customer issue: Customer bought an annual Business plan by mistake and asked for a refund 5 days after the charge.

Resolution: Eligible under the refund policy (annual plan, within 14 days). Support created a handoff; a billing team member approved the full refund, which reached the card in 7 business days.

title: Refund request for unused month on monthly plan
content:
Customer issue: Customer on a monthly Pro plan asked for a refund of the current month after cancelling.

Resolution: Not eligible: monthly plans are not refunded for partial or unused periods. Confirmed the cancellation takes effect at the end of the period with no further charges. The customer accepted.

title: Owner left company, cannot access account
content:
Customer issue: The workspace Owner left the company; remaining Admins needed ownership transferred.

Resolution: Self-service transfer requires the Owner. Escalated to a human support agent, who verified the company's identity with the documented verification process and transferred ownership to the requested Admin.

title: Password reset email not received
content:
Customer issue: User requested a password reset several times but got no email.

Resolution: The company mail filter quarantined mail from no-reply@cloudflow.example. IT allowed the sender, and the user requested one new link (limit 3 per hour) and reset the password. Support never handled the password.

title: Password reset not possible with SSO
content:
Customer issue: User couldn't reset their password from the CloudFlow login page.

Resolution: The workspace uses SAML SSO, so CloudFlow does not store the password. The user reset it with their company identity provider.

title: Locked out after lost 2FA device
content:
Customer issue: User lost their phone and recovery codes and couldn't sign in.

Resolution: A workspace Admin reset the user's 2FA from Settings > Team. The user signed in and set up 2FA again.

title: Runs rejected with CF-402
content:
Customer issue: All new runs were rejected with CF-402 near the end of the month.

Resolution: The Pro workspace had used all 25,000 monthly runs. Explained that the quota resets on the billing date and unused runs don't roll over. The customer upgraded to Business for a higher quota.

title: API usage close to limit
content:
Customer issue: Customer asked whether a peak of exactly 300 requests/min on Pro was a problem.

Resolution: Being exactly at the limit is allowed, but any burst above it returns 429. Recommended keeping headroom below the limit using X-RateLimit-Remaining and backoff.

title: GitHub webhook signature failures
content:
Customer issue: Webhook trigger returned 401 for requests from the customer's CI system.

Resolution: The CI system was signing with the old signing secret more than 24 hours after rotation. Customer updated the secret in CI; requests were accepted again.
